page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an AMD EPYC 7571 processor. Built on an x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual cores across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The memory subsystem consists of 64 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Storage is augmented by a dedicated 600 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, while network capacity provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results display modest compute throughput characteristic of first-generation AMD EPYC architecture. Single-core performance sits in the lower percentiles, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 722 and a stress-ng single-core score of 583.29. Multi-core operations scale effectively to middle-tier rankings, marked by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4662 and a PassMark CPU score of 12643.18. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 31.03 GB/sec for reads and 15.04 GB/sec for writes. The instance maintains dependable transactional efficiency, achieving 10.02 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and consistent results across PassMark database evaluations.

The primary tradeoff of the m5ad.4xlarge centers on lower per-thread compute performance versus balanced resource capacity and low-latency storage density. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage delivers economical data scratch space without incurring external block storage overhead. Given these parameters, this server type is functionally aligned with mid-tier relational databases, caching layers, batch data processing, build staging environments, and general enterprise workloads needing integrated NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.4xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server engineered for balanced workloads requiring fast local scratch storage. Driven by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, the configuration delivers 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) alongside 64 GB of DDR4 memory. High-speed IO is provided via a direct-attached 600 GB local NVMe SSD, backed by 5 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark data demonstrates modest single-thread compute capabilities alongside solid multi-core execution, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 12643.18 and processing 10.02 million Redis SET operations per second. While intensive single-threaded execution and heavy compression tasks show architectural limitations, the balanced core-to-memory ratio and bundled NVMe drive deliver reliable operational efficiency for intermediate databases, Redis caching layers, build runners, and enterprise back-office applications.
